label.retrieval: bounded text-only read, maximum 16384 bytes; no IMG requested
label.absence_interpretation: No declaration is not proof of no finite missing-value pixels.
label.description_inconsistency: Prose says approximately 60 m; structured grid says 0.236901 km/pixel.
label.digest_verification: Calculated during the single bounded read; original bytes not retained for independent rehash.

observations: Scaling reads band 1 without masked=True and uses src.nodata equality only.
No explicit read_masks/write_mask/mask-flag/alpha handling in alignment source. Rasterio/GDAL implicit mask behavior is not determined by this review.
Scaling copies profile but only explicitly updates dtype/compress/bigtiff; it does not explicitly set destination nodata to NaN or assign scales/offsets.
Reprojection uses the scaled source nodata metadata and destination NaN.
Nonempty scaled intermediates are reused; mere existence does not authenticate identity or generating code.
Slope generation uses aligned LOLA-only input when blended DEM is absent; actual historical choice is not independently verified.

next_readonly_receipt: Inventory existing labels/headers/receipts/logs only. Hash small labels, exported headers and receipts; for large rasters reuse existing authenticated hash receipts without reading whole rasters. Record present/absent and source versions; do not acquire rasters or rescan cohort.
For original, converted and scaled terrain inputs record observed nodata, mask flags and mask/alpha source, scale/offset, dtype and CRS/transform. Do not infer missing headers.

Trace cached-scaled reuse and generating tool versions/hashes through aligned/blended (or actual LOLA-only fallback)/slope/V1/V2/V4 records; record the actual slope input. Distinguish expected source from actual executed history.

If records cannot cover the fixed cohort, keep the guard closed. Propose separately scoped existing Train/Val window comparison only after a gap analysis, excluding Test and spatial halos that touch it; spot checks cannot prove full-cohort validity.
